To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a bicyclic mimetic for N-leucine was designed, synthesized and characterized; 2) constrained CCK/opioids containing this bicyclic diastereomer were prepared and tested; and 3) the constrained peptides were shown to have improved binding affinity and selectivity at the CCK receptors.

(1) the bicyclic diaminopropane mimetic for N-terminal amino acids is a potent CCK agonist, (2) the bicycyclic dipeptide mimics for Nle-Glu and Nle-Asn are weak CCK antagonists, and (3) the bicyciclic dipeptide mimic for homoPhe-Gln is a weak CCK agonist.

(i) bicyclic diastereoisomeric proline analogues of Nle-Asap have been synthesized, and (ii) the CCK and/or opioid receptor binding properties of constrained CCK/opioids containing the proline mimetic were not affected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of constrained analogues for CCK/opioids.
the development of constrained analogues that are designed to improve the pharmacology and bioavailability of CCK/opidoid chimeric peptide ligands.
the development of constrained analogues for CCK/opiodyl opioid chimeric peptides and their biological activity at both CCK and opioid receptor systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CCK receptor binding activity of the constrained analogues is not significantly affected, while the opioid receptor binding activity of these analogues is significantly reduced.
the CCK and/or opioid activities of the constrained chimeric peptide analogues are generally not affected by the presence of bicyclic diastereoisomers for Nle-asp or Nle-gly.
bicyclic diastereomers of the dipeptide mimics for Nle-asp and Nle-gly were found to be potent CCK agonists.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the constrained analogues containing the bicyclic diastereomers for Nle-Glu, Nle-Val, Nle-Arg, and Nle-Gly were more potent than the unconstrained analogues at the CCK receptor.
the bicyclic diastereomers were not as potent as the acyclic analogues, but the bicyclic analogues were more stable and more potent than the corresponding acyclic diastereomers.

the constrained CCK/opioids were more potent than the unconstrained CCK/opioids at the CCK receptor and less potent at the opioid receptors, but the constrained peptides were not more potent than the constrained peptides at both the CCR and opioid receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CCK and the opioid binding sites are not as tolerant of constrained peptide analogues as originally thought.

the CCK and δ-opioid receptors can be simultaneously targeted using CCK/opioids chimeric peptides containing a constrained dipeptide mimicking Nle-Aspr and that the bicyclic diastereomer is more active than the monocyclic analogues.
the bicyclic diastereomers are not as potent at the CCK receptor as the linear analogues, but the bicyclic analogues are more potent at the δ-opioid receptor than the linear analogues.
